title: The House of Vessel Farm
premise: When an excavation crew at Vessel Farm unearths a cellar door sealed from the inside, pest controller Odile Thackeray is called to investigate the 'infestation' — and discovers fingerprints on the walls that match her own. Trapped overnight with three surviving crew members, she learns the farmhouse was built as a vessel: a body for something the founding family invited in generations ago, fed by duty and kept docile by love. As dawn approaches, Odile must choose between destroying the house and sparing the last descendant, Merrit Vessel, whom she has come to love — knowing the thing inside has been wearing her memories like a coat. She burns the house with herself and Merrit inside it, but the final pages reveal the fire was also part of the invitation.
about_author: X. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former rural building inspector who spent a decade documenting structural failures in abandoned farmhouses across the Midwest. They write horror about architecture that remembers, and live in a house they refuse to describe.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: Odile Thackeray, POV. A routine call to Vessel Farm: scratching in the walls, a smell like wet copper. Odile, twenty years in pest control, catalogs rational explanations while noticing the scratches form patterns too deliberate for animals. The emotional beat is professional denial cracking at its first seam.

chapters.title: What the Excavator Found
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with crew foreman Dane Kowalczyk as secondary voice through his site log. The crew's digger strikes a stone stair beneath the barn; at its bottom, a door bolted from the inside, warm to the touch. One worker quits on the spot. The beat is dread arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Dusting the cellar walls for rodent tracks, she lifts prints that match her own — including a scar from a childhood injury. She tells no one. Flashbacks establish her twenty-year habit of explaining away noises, beginning with her grandmother's house. The beat is the collapse of her lifelong coping mechanism.

chapters.title: The Last Vessel
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, introducing Merrit Vessel, who arrives claiming ownership of land sold decades ago — papers impossible, face familiar from Odile's dreams. Merrit warns them to leave before dark and seems genuinely sorry. The beat is attraction entangled with warning, love and threat indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Sealed In
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At sunset every exit — doors, windows, the excavation shaft — closes as if grown over. Four remain: Odile, Dane, surveyor Priya Nair, and Merrit, who admits the house chose this night. The beat is claustrophobia and the group fracturing into blame.

chapters.title: The Family Record
chapters.summary: Merrit's POV. In the parlor, Merrit reads aloud from the Vessel ledger: in 1847 the family invited something in to survive a winter that killed everyone else, paying in generational service. Each heir was raised to love the house so the feeding would be willing. The beat is horror reframed as inheritance — duty as the trap itself.

chapters.title: What It Wants With Her
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The entity speaks through the walls using her grandmother's voice, revealing Odile's bloodline connects to the Vessels; the prints were hers because the house has been rehearsing her for years. Dane tries to burn it out and is taken. The beat is grief weaponized — the thing knows exactly how to be loved.

chapters.title: Sunrise Terms
chapters.summary: Odile and Merrit, alternating POV. The house offers a bargain: one willing vessel walks free at dawn if another stays. Priya flees into the walls and doesn't return. Odile realizes Merrit has been groomed since birth to volunteer, and that loving Merrit may be the entity's oldest trick. The beat is love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Door From the Inside
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax. She descends to the sealed door, now unbolted, and finds behind it not a monster but a room of waiting versions of herself. Understanding the invitation requires consent, she sets the fire anyway — taking Merrit's hand, refusing the choice the house designed. The beat is defiance: survival priced at everything.

chapters.title: Ashes, Willing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, then a cold epistolary coda. The farm burns; investigators find two sets of remains holding hands, and one set of bare footprints leading away. Odile wakes in a motel room she doesn't remember checking into, her reflection a half-second late. The beat is ambiguous survival — the price paid, and possibly collected.
